articles.title: AAP Sarpanch Shot Dead at Wedding in Amritsar, Second High-Profile Killing in Punjab in Four Days
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Jarnail Singh, also reported as Jarmal Singh, a sarpanch from Valtoha village in Tarn Taran district and a member of the ruling Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), was shot dead on Sunday, January 5, 2026, at a wedding venue in Amritsar.

body.html:
Jarnail Singh, also reported as Jarmal Singh, a sarpanch from Valtoha village in Tarn Taran district and a member of the ruling Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), was shot dead on Sunday, January 5, 2026, at a wedding venue in Amritsar.

The incident occurred at the Marigold Resort wedding hall, where Singh had gone to attend a relative’s marriage. According to police, unidentified gunmen entered the venue and fired two shots at the back of his head. Panic broke out among guests, and Singh was rushed to a nearby hospital, where he succumbed to his injuries during treatment.

Amritsar Deputy Commissioner of Police Jagjeet Walia said the attackers appeared to have specifically targeted Singh. Police are scanning CCTV footage from the venue and nearby areas. All angles are being probed, including reports that Singh had received threats from gangsters in the past. No arrests have been made so far.

Reacting to the incident, Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) chief Sukhbir Singh Badal termed the killing a “cold-blooded murder” and blamed what he called a failure of policing in Punjab. He linked the incident to other recent violent crimes in the state, including a murder in Moga and a shooting in Kapurthala.

The killing has sent shockwaves through Punjab’s political circles and has raised serious concerns over rising targeted violence in public places. Investigations are ongoing.

articles.title: Man Arrested in UP’s Baghpat for Forcibly Feeding Liquor to Stray Dog; Video Goes Viral
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Baghpat police have arrested a man after a disturbing video showing a stray dog being forcibly fed liquor went viral on social media. The incident took place in Kirthal village under Ramala police station limits.

body.html:
Baghpat police have arrested a man after a disturbing video showing a stray dog being forcibly fed liquor went viral on social media. The incident took place in Kirthal village under Ramala police station limits.

The accused, identified as Jitendra alias Ballam, was seen in the viral clip cruelly administering alcohol to a dog from a liquor bottle. The video was taken cognisance of by the Social Media Cell of Baghpat Police, following which Ramala police identified and arrested the accused.

An FIR (No. 5/2026) has been registered at Ramala police station under Section 3/11(1)(c) of the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act. Police said necessary legal action is being taken.

Baghpat Police have issued a warning stating that cruelty towards animals will not be tolerated and strict action will be taken against offenders.

Arrested Accused:
Jitendra alias Ballam, son of Jaipal Singh, resident of Kirthal village, Ramala police station area, Baghpat district.

Arresting Team:
Inspector Jitendra Kumar
Sub-Inspector Yuvnish Kumar
(Ramala Police Station, Baghpat)

articles.title: UP Shocker: Woman Elopes With Nephew, Leaves 3-Year-Old Daughter Behind in Deoria
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A shocking incident has surfaced from Sohanpur village in Deoria district, where a married woman allegedly eloped with her nephew, leaving behind her three-year-old daughter.

body.html:
A shocking incident has surfaced from Sohanpur village in Deoria district, where a married woman allegedly eloped with her nephew, leaving behind her three-year-old daughter. The woman’s husband, Mannu Gupta (31), who works as a mechanic in Saudi Arabia, returned to India after learning about the incident and filed a complaint with the police.

According to the complaint, Mannu returned on December 29 after being informed by his brother. He alleged that his wife, Pooja Devi, left the house on the night of December 24 and took jewellery and cash worth nearly ₹10 lakh.

Mannu stated that he married Pooja four years ago and that the couple has a young daughter. He alleged that Pooja had been in a relationship with her nephew, Chandan Gupta, for the past two years. Mannu claimed he had tried multiple times to counsel her but was ignored. He further alleged that she openly posted pictures with Chandan on social media.

Family members said they had earlier warned Pooja. Mannu’s elder brother reportedly caught Pooja and Chandan in a compromising situation in the past, but the family chose to remain silent due to social pressure. Chandan reportedly lives barely 150 metres from Mannu’s house.

Mannu alleged that while he was working abroad, he regularly sent money home, including savings meant for his daughter’s future, which were taken when Pooja left.

The abandoned child is currently staying with relatives, as Mannu said the situation at home is emotionally distressing. Villagers have strongly condemned the incident, calling it cruel to leave a young child behind.

Police confirmed that a missing person report has been registered at Bankata police station. Station in-charge Vishal Kumar Upadhyay said efforts are underway to trace the woman and the youth. Further legal action will be taken once they are located and statements are recorded.

articles.title: Exorcism Turns Deadly: Mother Gets Suspended Jail Term After Daughter Dies in ‘Demon Ritual
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A tragic case driven by superstition has shocked China, after a court in southern China found a woman guilty of causing her daughter’s death during a failed home “exorcism.” The court ruled there was no intent to kill, but the ritual directly led to the young woman’s death.

body.html:
A tragic case driven by superstition has shocked China, after a court in southern China found a woman guilty of causing her daughter’s death during a failed home “exorcism.” The court ruled there was no intent to kill, but the ritual directly led to the young woman’s death.

A Shenzhen court in Guangdong province sentenced the mother, surnamed Li, to three years in prison, suspended for four years. Her elder daughter, who took part in the ritual, received the same sentence. Both were convicted of negligent homicide, with the verdict delivered in July.

According to the South China Morning Post, the court noted that the accused cooperated with investigators, admitted their wrongdoing and showed remorse, which led to suspended sentences instead of immediate imprisonment.

The court found that Li and her two daughters were deeply influenced by extreme superstitious beliefs, including ideas of demonic possession and supernatural attacks. In December last year, the younger daughter, surnamed Xie, claimed she was possessed and demanded an exorcism.

During the ritual, the mother and elder sister pressed on her chest and forced water down her throat, believing it would expel the “evil spirit.” The victim reportedly urged them to continue, but she was found unconscious and bleeding from the mouth the next morning. She was declared dead at the scene.

The court said blind belief in superstition and lack of medical knowledge led to fatal negligence, stressing that personal beliefs cannot justify actions that endanger life.

articles.title: Kolar Shocker: Man Held for Late-Night Thefts of Women’s Innerwear, Police Stunned by Discovery
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A disturbing incident from the Kolar area of the capital has shocked residents and police alike. Authorities have arrested a young man accused of breaking into homes late at night and stealing women’s innerwear. The condition in which the accused was found left even the police surprised.

body.html:
A disturbing incident from the Kolar area of the capital has shocked residents and police alike. Authorities have arrested a young man accused of breaking into homes late at night and stealing women’s innerwear. The condition in which the accused was found left even the police surprised.

The incident occurred around 12:30 AM. on Tuesday night in Amarnath Colony, Kolar. A dairy businessman noticed suspicious movement on his balcony and stepped out after sensing something unusual. On raising an alarm, he saw a young man fleeing with women’s clothing.

During the escape, the accused dropped his labour card at the spot, which led to his identification as Dipesh. Based on the complaint and the document recovered from the scene, Kolar police conducted a raid at the accused’s residence on Wednesday.

When police reached the house, they found Dipesh sleeping. Officers were shocked to discover that he was wearing the stolen women’s innerwear. He was immediately detained, and further investigation was initiated.

Following the revelation, the incident has become a major topic of discussion in Amarnath Colony and nearby areas. Police are now examining whether the accused suffers from a mental health condition or if he has been involved in similar incidents earlier.

Police officials stated that the accused has been arrested and that the evidence and circumstances suggest abnormal behaviour. Further legal action is underway as the investigation continues.

articles.title: Honeytrap Racket Busted in Barmer: Woman, Accomplice Caught Extorting Lawyer With Obscene Video
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A honeytrap and extortion racket has been exposed in Barmer district of Rajasthan, where police arrested two accused while they were allegedly accepting ₹50,000 from a local lawyer as part of a ₹40 lakh extortion demand.

body.html:
A honeytrap and extortion racket has been exposed in Barmer district of Rajasthan, where police arrested two accused while they were allegedly accepting ₹50,000 from a local lawyer as part of a ₹40 lakh extortion demand.

The arrested accused have been identified as Kamal Singh, a resident of Barmer, and Priyanka, originally from West Bengal. According to police, the victim, advocate Prem Kumar, lodged a complaint at Barmer Kotwali police station after being blackmailed with an obscene video.

As per the complaint, Priyanka, who had earlier worked at a spa in Balotra, shifted to Roy Colony in Barmer and befriended the lawyer at a local gym. She allegedly lured him to her room, where an obscene video was secretly recorded using a spy camera. The accused later threatened to make the video viral and file a false rape case unless a large sum of money was paid.

Police said Kamal Singh was tasked with collecting the extortion money. Fearing damage to his reputation, the lawyer initially paid part of the demanded amount. He later informed the police, following which a trap was laid.

During the operation, police caught Kamal Singh and Priyanka red-handed while accepting ₹50,000 from the victim. The cash was seized, and both accused were taken into custody.

Barmer Kotwali police have registered a case under relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita related to extortion and criminal intimidation. The court has remanded both accused to two days of police custody for further interrogation.

Police said investigations are underway to determine whether the accused are part of a larger honeytrap gang and to examine digital evidence and possible involvement in similar cases.

articles.title: Wife Plots Husband’s Murder With Lover, Body Dumped in 50-Foot Pit; ‘Spirit Drama’ Used to Mislead
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A shocking case of murder has been uncovered in Dholpur district, where a woman allegedly conspired with her lover to kill her husband and dump his body in a deep pit near Shergarh Fort.

body.html:
A shocking case of murder has been uncovered in Dholpur district, where a woman allegedly conspired with her lover to kill her husband and dump his body in a deep pit near Shergarh Fort. The victim, Ravikant Singh (34), was reportedly forced to consume alcohol before being brutally killed with a stone.

Ravikant, a resident of Daunari village under the Sainpau police station area, worked as a daily wage labourer in Bengaluru to support his family. He was married around 14 years ago to Rajni (32), a resident of Hathwari village. The couple has a seven-year-old daughter and a five-year-old son.

According to police, Rajni developed a relationship about a year ago with Shahrukh (20), an auto driver from Sainpau. During interrogation, Shahrukh revealed that he first met Rajni at Dholpur railway station when she had come to drop her husband off to Bengaluru. After repeated meetings, the two allegedly entered into a love affair.

Shahrukh told police that Ravikant returned from Bengaluru on December 26 and came home in his auto. He stayed at Ravikant’s house that night and left the next morning. He further claimed that Rajni repeatedly pressured him to kill her husband.

As per the confession, Rajni convinced Ravikant to go shopping with Shahrukh on December 27. Following the plan, Shahrukh took Ravikant on a bike to Shergarh Fort. There, behind a temple, he allegedly made Ravikant drink alcohol and, after he was intoxicated, struck his head twice with a large stone, killing him on the spot. The body was then dumped into a pit around 50 feet deep.

When Ravikant did not return home, his cousin Sanjay Kumar filed a missing person report on December 27. On December 29, Rajni allegedly tried to mislead the family by claiming that her husband’s spirit had possessed her. She took family members near Shergarh Fort, where they found her blood-stained chunri and a blood-stained stone. During a search outside the fort wall, police recovered Ravikant’s body from a pit, with his head and face crushed.

Dholpur SP Vikas Sangwan confirmed that the murder took place on the evening of December 29 and that the case was cracked after Shahrukh’s interrogation. Kotwali police station in-charge Virendra Meena said forensic teams were called to the spot and evidence was collected.

After the recovery of the body, Rajni fled the area. Police arrested Shahrukh, who confessed to the crime. Efforts are underway to trace and arrest Rajni, who remains absconding.

articles.title: Retired Railway Clerk Dies of Neglect, Disabled Daughter Found Starved After 5 Years of Captivity
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A horrific case of prolonged abuse and neglect has come to light in Mahoba district of Uttar Pradesh, where a 70-year-old retired railway clerk died under suspicious circumstances, while his mentally challenged daughter was found in a severely emaciated condition after allegedly being...

body.html:
A horrific case of prolonged abuse and neglect has come to light in Mahoba district of Uttar Pradesh, where a 70-year-old retired railway clerk died under suspicious circumstances, while his mentally challenged daughter was found in a severely emaciated condition after allegedly being confined for five years by their caretakers.

The deceased has been identified as Omprakash Singh Rathore, a retired railway employee. His 27-year-old daughter, Rashmi, who is mentally challenged, was rescued in a critical condition. The incident surfaced on December 29, 2025, after relatives were informed about Omprakash’s death and rushed to the house.

According to family members, Omprakash shifted to a separate house with Rashmi after his wife’s death in 2016. Around the same time, Ram Prakash Kushwaha and his wife Ramdevi were hired as caretakers. Over the years, the couple allegedly took control of the house, confining Omprakash and Rashmi to ground-floor rooms while occupying the upper floors themselves.

Relatives alleged that the caretakers denied the father and daughter proper food, medical treatment, and access to visitors. They reportedly turned away family members using various excuses. The motive behind the abuse is suspected to be the illegal control of the victim’s property and assets.

When relatives reached the house following Omprakash’s death, they found his body extremely weak and emaciated. Rashmi was discovered naked in a dark room, starved to a skeletal condition and barely able to move. Family members said her physical condition made her appear decades older than her actual age.

Omprakash was taken to hospital, where doctors declared him brought dead. The post-mortem report indicated chronic lung disease, though the family alleges prolonged neglect contributed to his death.

Rashmi has since been taken into the care of relatives and is undergoing recovery. Police have launched an investigation into the matter. As of the latest update, no arrests have been reported. The family has demanded strict action against the accused caretakers.

articles.title: Hospital Bed Allegations Shake Dharamshala College: 19-Year-Old Student’s Death Raises Troubling Q
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A 19-year-old BA student, Pallavi, from Siddhawadi near Dharamshala, died on December 26 while on oxygen support.

body.html:
A 19-year-old BA student, Pallavi, from Siddhawadi near Dharamshala, died on December 26 while on oxygen support. Before her death, she made serious allegations against a geology professor and several fellow students of Dharamshala Degree College, accusing them of molestation, ragging, mental torture and assault.

Pallavi had failed her first-year exam in July 2025 by one mark and was later expelled. When she sought re-admission in September, she was advised to apply for re-evaluation. She alleged that a professor insulted her and forced her out of the classroom, after which she stopped attending college and slipped into severe depression.

Her family claimed Pallavi was beaten and harassed by students. Despite treatment in Dharamshala, Tanda, Pathankot and Ludhiana, her condition worsened and she became bedridden by October. Complaints were made to the Chief Minister’s Helpline, and a video statement was recorded. Police visited on December 21, but could not record her statement due to her critical condition.

Videos of Pallavi on oxygen support went viral on January 1, in which she accused Professor Ashok Kumar of inappropriate touching and mental torture. In another video, however, she described the same professor as “good,” leading to confusion. The college administration and some students denied the allegations, claiming there were no written complaints and that her distress was linked to academic failure.

The family has alleged negligence by the police and administration, pointing out that no post-mortem was conducted. An SC/ST angle has also been raised, though the accused professor belongs to the Dalit community.

Following a complaint by Pallavi’s father, police have registered a case against three students and one professor under charges of harassment, indecent touch and assault. The UGC has ordered a separate inquiry and constituted a fact-finding committee. The investigation is ongoing.

articles.title: iPhone Snatched at Assi Ghat, Mumbai Woman Tracks Thief Herself; Cache of Stolen Phones Recovered
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Varanasi witnessed a dramatic turn of events after a mobile phone theft at Assi Ghat during the New Year holiday rush. A young man allegedly snatched an iPhone worth nearly ₹2 lakh from Ankita Gupta, a software engineer from Mumbai, and fled amid the heavy crowd.

body.html:
Varanasi witnessed a dramatic turn of events after a mobile phone theft at Assi Ghat during the New Year holiday rush. A young man allegedly snatched an iPhone worth nearly ₹2 lakh from Ankita Gupta, a software engineer from Mumbai, and fled amid the heavy crowd.

Despite the large gathering at the ghat, Ankita alleged that security arrangements were absent. She immediately approached the police and submitted a complaint along with the mobile bill, documents and EMI details. However, she claimed that the police failed to trace the phone’s location or identify the accused.

Taking matters into her own hands, Ankita used a mobile tracking application to trace the device. With the help of local residents, she began searching for the suspect. Early the next morning, around 5 am, she returned to the area and traced the location to a rented house on GT Road.

With the landlord’s assistance, the locked room was opened. Although the accused had fled, 15 to 20 expensive mobile phones were recovered from inside. Ankita immediately identified her stolen iPhone among them. She stayed at the spot till around 2 am and informed the police.

Police later arrived at the scene and seized all the recovered mobile phones. Bhelupur Inspector Sudhir Tripathi said that raids are underway to arrest the accused and further investigation is in progress.

The incident has gone viral on social media, with many praising Ankita Gupta’s presence of mind and courage. Locals in Varanasi have also lauded her determination, calling the episode an example of how alert citizens can help expose crime even when response systems are slow.
